ingredientSections.heading: Beef Jus
items: 1 Tbsp beef fat or bone marrow

methodSections.heading: Fermented Horseradish (3 weeks in advance)
steps: Bring the water to a boil and then dissolve the salt in it to create a brine. Allow to cool. Sanitize a mason jar or similar in boiling water. Allow to cool.
Peel the horseradish, chop it into 2-3cm (1 in) pieces and place in the mason jar. Wear gloves to avoid bacteria transfer from your hands and do this in a ventilated area.
Cover the horseradish in the brine until it is completely submerged. Use a sanitized weight to stop it from floating if necessary.
Cover the jar with cheesecloth and let sit 3 weeks. Top up with some of the remaining brine if the level lowers in this time.
Remove the horseradish from the brine and blend until creamy.

methodSections.heading: Rosemary Oil
steps: Strip the rosemary leaves and pick off the thick part of the parsley stems.
Blend all ingredients in a blender for 10 min.

methodSections.heading: Cauliflower Purée
steps: Remove the cauliflower stalks and reserve them for the Pickled Cauliflower (below). Cut the florets into similar sized portions.
Bring the butter to a foam in a saucepan with the salt and then add and soften cauliflower.
Almost fully cover the cauliflower in the cream and then stir in the horseradish. Tightly cover the saucepan with plastic-wrap and cook over a low medium heat until completely cooked and soft.
Blend the cooked cauliflower and cream on high in a blender and then pass it through a fine mesh strainer. Season to taste.

methodSections.heading: Pickled Cauliflower
steps: Slice the cauliflower thinly on a mandoline and lay out on tray or plate.
Lightly sprinkle with salt and leave for 20 minutes.
Drizzle a splash of chardonnay vinegar evenly over the cauliflower.

methodSections.heading: Beef Jus
steps: Warm the jus and fat together and emulsify with a hand blender.

methodSections.heading: Pomme Anna
steps: In a frying pan clarify the butter with both the rosemary and thyme and then strain reserving the butter.
Slice potatoes thinly on mandoline and chop the shallots very finely.
In large bowl, add and mix through with your fingers just enough cornstarch to the potatoes so they start to feel silky.
Layer potatoes and shallots to around 4cm (1½in) thick in a criss-cross pattern in a small oven safe dish.
Cover in the butter and, with a lid on, bake in an oven preheated to 150°C (300°F) for approximately 30 minutes or until just tender.
Press the potatoes with a weight (a large can or a stack of plates) in the fridge until cool.

methodSections.heading: Elk Loin and Serving
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Cut the cauliflower into equal florets and blanch until beginning to soften.
Season and then sear the elk lightly on all sides, and place in the oven for about 8-10 minutes or until medium rare. Allow to rest for at least 8 minutes.
While the elk is resting, cut the pressed Pomme Anna into serving-sized cubes and sear with the cauliflower florets in butter until golden brown.
Once hot, melt some more butter in another pan and flash fry the elk in it.
To build the plate, start with a smear of the Cauliflower Purée, then arrange the Pomme Anna, pickled and seared cauliflower.
Slice the elk into 2 pieces against the grain of the meat, season the cut sides with salt, and place on the plate.
Pour some of the Beef Jus over the meat and finish with the Rosemary Oil.
